concept_posts.post_content:
Ever tried searching a product description table with LIKE and ended up scanning millions of rows?
I felt the same until I discovered PostgreSQL's full‑text search.
It lets you index textual data the way search engines do,
so queries become lightning fast.

Imagine you have a table articles(id, title, body) and you want to find anything about "data pipelines".
You create a tsvector column from title and body,
add a GIN index,
then query with to_tsquery('data & pipeline').
PostgreSQL does the heavy lifting,
ranking results by relevance.

Key takeaways:
- Use tsvector and GIN indexes to make searches efficient.
- Leverage language dictionaries to handle stemming and stop words.
- Combine ts_rank_cd with ORDER BY to surface the most relevant rows.

Common mistake: forgetting to update the tsvector column when the source text changes,
which leads to stale search results.

What’s the most surprising thing you’ve learned about full‑text search in PostgreSQL?
